title: AI Literacy in K-12 and Higher Education in the Wake of Generative AI: An Integrative Review
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly expanding and poorly defined area of AI literacy education in the wake of generative AI. The authors ask how researchers conceptualize AI literacy in K-12 and higher education and what new trends have emerged since generative AI became publicly available. Their goal is not to evaluate a single intervention, but to synthesize the field and build a framework that clarifies the different ways AI literacy is being defined and taught.

The study uses an integrative review approach to examine 124 empirical and theoretical studies published between 2020 and July 2024. The review focuses on K-12 and undergraduate contexts and excludes graduate, adult, and discipline-specific professional training. The authors code each study by how it conceptualizes AI and literacy, identifying three AI perspectives (technical details, tools, sociocultural impact) and three literacy perspectives (functional, critical, indirectly beneficial). They then map how these combine across studies, including pre-generative-AI curricula centered on machine learning or AI ethics and post-generative-AI work emphasizing direct use of tools such as ChatGPT.

The review finds that AI literacy research has shifted notably after generative AI, with a sharp increase in studies focused on AI tools and prompt engineering, especially in higher education. In K-12, most studies still emphasize machine learning fundamentals and ethics, often combining technical and sociocultural content. The paper concludes that AI literacy is too broad a term for the current landscape and argues for more precise terminology that distinguishes technical, tool-based, ethical, and indirectly beneficial goals. It also identifies gaps, especially around critical and sociocultural use of AI tools and around comparable post-secondary curricula.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic category of generative AI / large language model tools used for language-based interaction, content generation, prompting, and instruction support, without a single named commercial product being the focus.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is an integrative review of AI literacy studies in K-12 and higher education. It synthesizes how recent studies conceptualize AI literacy in the wake of generative AI, including studies that discuss or teach use of ChatGPT and other generative AI tools, but it does not empirically evaluate one specific tool.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an integrative review and conceptual framework paper, not a primary empirical evaluation of a tool. It synthesizes prior studies rather than reporting a single study design with tool-level outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct outcome effects are reported for a specific AI tool, so there is no measurable intervention impact to rate. The paper is useful for framing the literature, but not for estimating student outcome gains.
